Also save a few sample frames around suspected jump frames for visual inspection. This should give cleaner y-position data to identify takeoff and landing.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "python3 - <<'PY'
import cv2, numpy as np, os
cap=cv2.VideoCapture('/app/example_video.mp4')
frames=[]
while True:
    ret, frame=cap.read()
    if not ret: break
    frames.append(frame)
cap.release()
print('total', len(frames))
os.makedirs('/app/debug_frames', exist_ok=True)
prev=None
for i, frame in enumerate(frames):
    gray=cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    if prev is None:
        prev=gray
        print(f'{i:3d} no prev')
        continue
    diff=np.abs(gray.astype(np.int16)-prev.astype(np.int16))
    mask=(diff>20).astype(np.uint8)*255
    mask=cv2.morphologyEx(mask, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, np.ones((3,3),np.uint8))
    mask=cv2.morphologyEx(mask, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, np.ones((9,9),np.uint8))
    contours,_=cv2.findContours(mask, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    if not contours:
        print(f'{i:3d} no contours')
        prev=gray
        continue
    c=max(contours, key=cv2.contourArea)
    area=cv2.contourArea(c)
    x,y,w,h=cv2.boundingRect(c)
    if area>100:
        print(f'{i:3d} area={area:7.0f} x={x:4d} y={y:4d} w={w:4d} h={h:4d} bot={y+h:4d} top={y:4d} cx={x+w//2:4d}')
    else:
        print(f'{i:3d} area={area:7.0f} too small')
    if i in [0,5,20,40,47,48,49,50,55,60,65,70,71,72,75,80,85,90,95,100,105,110,115,119]:
        cv2.imwrite(f'/app/debug_frames/frame_{i:03d}.jpg', frame)
        cv2.imwrite(f'/app/debug_frames/mask_{i:03d}.jpg', mask)
    prev=gray
PY
